triage.rulebook_article: FIA Driving Standards Guidelines §2.1 - Overtaking at Corner Entry
triage.justification: Attacking car HAMILTON executed an uncontrolled divebomb into the corner apex, carrying excessive closing velocity (40.3 km/h) with rapid lateral convergence (10.7 m/s) and causing contact with defending driver NORRIS (AI).

bulletin.headline: DECISION: CAR (HAMILTON) PENALTY
bulletin.infringement: FIA Driving Standards Guidelines §2.1 - Overtaking at Corner Entry
bulletin.facts: At timestamp t=19.65s during the session, Car HAMILTON and Car NORRIS (AI) converged to a minimum center separation of 2.74m. Synchronized 20Hz telemetry recorded a longitudinal closing velocity of 40.3 km/h, an along-track gap of 2.53m, and a lateral clearance of 1.07m. Lateral convergence rate was 10.70 m/s with a chassis overlap ratio of 54.9%. Physical contact was established at t=19.65s.
bulletin.reasoning: The Stewards reviewed telemetry data, tracking radar projections, and GPS coordinate feeds. The evidence demonstrates that Car HAMILTON was wholly or predominantly to blame for the incident. Attacking car HAMILTON executed an uncontrolled divebomb into the corner apex, carrying excessive closing velocity (40.3 km/h) with rapid lateral convergence (10.7 m/s) and causing contact with defending driver NORRIS (AI). The Stewards determine that this constitutes a breach of FIA Driving Standards Guidelines §2.1 - Overtaking at Corner Entry. Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and Chapter 4 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.
